question: For the same stated lossless parameters L′=250 nH/m and C′=100 pF/m, find propagation speed in units of 10⁸ m/s.

steps: The product is 2.5×10⁻¹⁷ s²/m².
Its square root is 5×10⁻⁹ s/m.
Speed is 2×10⁸ m/s, so enter 2 in requested units.

question: A lossless short-circuited line has Z0=50 Ω and length λ/8. Find the imaginary part of Zin in ohms.

steps: At λ/8 the electrical length is π/4.
tan(π/4)=1, giving Zin=j50 Ω.
Its imaginary part is +50 Ω, inductive under the stated phasor convention.
solution.explanation: Its imaginary part is +50 Ω, inductive under the stated phasor convention.
commonMistakes: A shorted stub need not look like a short away from zero or half-wavelength lengths.

hints: Identify the conditions under which shorted-stub impedance applies.
Start from $ Z_{in}=jZ_0\tan(\beta l) $.

verification.method: Evaluate shorted-stub input reactance at the actual electrical length. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: A lossless open-circuited line has Z0=50 Ω and length λ/8. Find the imaginary part of Zin in ohms.

steps: The open termination produces the cotangent form.
cot(π/4)=1, so Zin=−j50 Ω.
The imaginary part is −50 Ω, capacitive.
solution.explanation: The imaginary part is −50 Ω, capacitive.
commonMistakes: Open and shorted stubs have different reactance functions and signs.

hints: Identify the conditions under which open-stub impedance applies.

question: A line has |Γ|=0.1 at the load. Find return loss −20log₁₀|Γ| in dB.

solution.asked: Convert reflection coefficient to return loss.
steps: log₁₀0.1=−1.

Return loss is 20 dB; higher positive return loss means smaller reflection.

question: A lossless line has normalized load zL=1+j relative to real Z0. Find the imaginary part of ΓL.

steps: The ratio is j/(2+j).
Multiply numerator and denominator by 2−j to obtain (1+2j)/5.
The imaginary part is 2/5=0.4, while the real part is 0.2.

hints: Identify the conditions under which smith-plane reflection mapping applies.

question: For an ideal passive resistive load ZL>0 on a lossless real-Z0 line, its reflection coefficient lies:

options.text: On the real axis strictly between −1 and +1

given: Finite strictly positive real ZL and Z0
steps: The ratio of real quantities is real.
Since both resistances are positive, the numerator magnitude is strictly less than the denominator.
Thus −1<Γ<1 on the real axis, option B.
solution.explanation: Thus −1<Γ<1 on the real axis, option B.
commonMistakes: The endpoints correspond to zero or infinite resistance limits, excluded here.

hints: Identify the conditions under which passive-resistance reflection locus applies.
Start from $ \Gamma=(R_L-Z_0)/(R_L+Z_0) $.

verification.method: Algebraic positivity bound |R−Z0|<R+Z0 for finite positive real resistances. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: A forward traveling voltage wave decays as e⁻ᵅˡ on a matched lossy line. If α=0.1 Np/m and l=10 m, find output/input power ratio.

steps: The voltage amplitude attenuation is e⁻¹.
Power is proportional to its squared magnitude in the same normalization.
The power ratio is e⁻²≈0.1353352832.
commonMistakes: A nepers-per-meter amplitude attenuation doubles its exponent when converted to power.

hints: Identify the conditions under which voltage versus power attenuation applies.
Start from $ P_{out}/P_{in}=e^{-2\alpha l} $.

verification.method: Attenuate forward wave amplitude, then square its magnitude for power. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Adjacent voltage maxima on a lossless standing-wave line are measured 0.4 m apart. Find the guided wavelength in meters.

steps: The standing-wave envelope repeats each half wavelength.
The measured adjacent-maxima separation is 0.4 m.
Therefore λ=2×0.4=0.8 m.
commonMistakes: Neighboring maximum and minimum are λ/4 apart; two maxima are λ/2 apart.

hints: Identify the conditions under which standing-wave spatial periodicity applies.
Start from $ \Delta l_{max}=\lambda/2 $.

verification.method: Standing-wave maxima repeat every π of βl, equivalent to half wavelength. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: On a lossless line, the reflection coefficient at distance l toward the generator is Γin=ΓL exp(−j2βl). For ΓL=1 and l=λ/8, find Im Γin.

steps: The round-trip phase rotation is −π/2.
Multiplying ΓL=1 by e⁻ʲπᐟ² yields −j.
The imaginary part is −1.
commonMistakes: The reflection coefficient accumulates twice the one-way propagation phase.

hints: Identify the conditions under which round-trip reflection phase applies.
Start from $ 2\beta l=2(2\pi/\lambda)(\lambda/8)=\pi/2 $.

verification.method: Compute double-pass complex phase rotation and extract imaginary component. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Which statements about an ideal matched lossless line section are true?

options.text: Its input impedance equals Z0 for any length when terminated in Z0
Its transmitted-wave magnitude is unchanged along the section
It introduces zero phase delay at every frequency regardless of length
The line can introduce propagation delay without reflecting a wave

steps: A matched load removes the backward wave, leaving the same V/I ratio Z0 everywhere.
Losslessness preserves traveling-wave magnitude.
The phase factor can still produce delay, so phase need not be zero. Select A,B,D.
solution.explanation: The phase factor can still produce delay, so phase need not be zero. Select A,B,D.
commonMistakes: Absence of reflection is not absence of propagation time.

hints: Identify the conditions under which matched traveling waves applies.
Start from $ \Gamma_L=0,\quad V^+(l)=V^+(0)e^{-j\beta l} $.

verification.method: Matched lossless traveling-wave solution, magnitude preservation and nonzero phase accumulation. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.
